Will the drive into downtown be a problem tomorrow morning? This dashboard answers that one question for people who work in downtown Buffalo. It pulls the National Weather Service forecast every few hours and rates each weekday commute window, by direction of travel, as Low, Elevated, High, or Severe.

## How the rating works

{{< include _method.html >}}

## Why by corridor

Lake effect snow is narrow. A band off Lake Erie can bury Orchard Park while downtown and Amherst see flurries, and a few hours later it can swing north. A single "Buffalo" forecast hides that, so each corridor is rated on the worst conditions at either end of the trip.

## The data

All data comes from the [National Weather Service API](https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api), which is free and public. For each forecast point the script pulls:

- snowfall and ice accumulation
- wind gusts
- "feels like" temperature
- active winter weather alerts

A Python script converts the forecast to hourly values, totals them for the morning (6 to 9 a.m.) and evening (4 to 7 p.m.) commute windows, applies the thresholds above, and writes the dashboard. GitHub Actions reruns it on a schedule, so the page stays current without anyone touching it.

## Limits

- **Lake effect bands are hard to place.** A shift of a few miles changes which corridor is hit, so treat the ratings as guidance.
- **Snow and ice amounts are only forecast a few days ahead.** Later windows are rated on wind, cold, and alerts alone, and are marked.
- **Travel bans and road closures are not included.** Those come from Erie County and the City of Buffalo.
- **The thresholds are my own judgment**, informed by forecasting experience. They have not yet been tested against past storms.

## What's next

- Test the ratings against past events, such as the November and December 2022 storms.
- Compare each forecast with what fell, to show how reliable the outlook is at one, two, and three days out.
